page.name: Customer feedback requests
page.h1: Ask for feedback without becoming noise
page.metaDescription: Post-transaction feedback requests sent with suppression applied, a one-question format, and a real send-time decision.
page.lede: A feedback request is marketing in everything but name, so treat it like one: one question, sent once, to people who have not opted out. That is what keeps the answers worth reading.

bullets: A rating with a single tap
An optional free-text box, not a required one
A clear statement of what the feedback changes
A link to a longer survey for the minority who want it
p: The response rate collapses with every additional question, and the answers stop being comparable. A short request sent consistently produces better data than a thorough one sent rarely.

sections.h: It is promotional traffic — suppression applies
p: A feedback request is promotional traffic, so opt-out suppression on the SMS channel applies — a customer who asked not to be marketed to should not be surveyed. The platform applies the suppression it is configured with, per the rules you set.
bullets: Opt-out keywords matched exactly, so a request is never silently swallowed by a loose match
Re-subscription handled deliberately rather than implicitly

sections.h: Time it after the transaction resolves
p: The best moment is shortly after the transaction resolves and long enough afterwards that the customer has an opinion. That is a product decision; the platform sends when told to send, and logs what happened.

faq.a: Yes — they are promotional traffic, and suppression on the SMS channel applies to them.
Scheduled and bulk sending are console features. Scheduling a feedback run days after a transaction is a configuration rather than a code change.

faq.q: Will a “STOP” in a normal reply suppress someone?
faq.a: Opt-out keywords are matched exactly rather than fuzzily, precisely so that collateral wording does not silently suppress a customer.
